the degradation of the base-emitter junction is the dominant degradation mechanism in InGaAs/ InP DHBT under both thermal and electrical stresses, and the degradation of the current gain β can be modeled by a thermally activated process with an activation energy of around 1.1 eV.

the base–emiter junction degradation has been observed in InGaAs/ InP DHBT under both electrical and thermal stresses.

the reliability of InP DHBT technology for high-speed ICs applications.
the study of the reliability of InP/InGaAs DHBT technology.
the study of the reliability of submicron HBTs under thermal and electrical stress.

the base–emiter junction is the weakest part in the InGaAs/ InP DHBT technology.
the base–emiter junction is the weakest link of the InGaAs/ InP DHBT.

the reliability of our HBT technology is comparable to that of the best InP HBT technology reported in the literature.
the InGaAs/ InP HBT is reliable under the thermal and electrical stress considered here.

the reliability of submicron DHBT is not degraded by the high current densities.
the base current degradation is the limiting factor in the reliability of InP DHBT technology for high-speed applications.
